notes.meaning: God gives new directions to Moses from the pillar of cloud. Israel was on the edge of the desert, but the Lord now tells Moses to guide the people into an unexpected turn of direction. This shows that God leads His people step by step according to His own plan.

God tells Israel to turn off their direct route and set up camp between the rocky defiles and the sea. Humanly speaking, this was a dangerous move because it penned them in with water in front and mountains on their sides. God deliberately guided them into this difficult spot so that He could display His power when He brought them out.

God explains that Pharaoh will think the Israelites have lost their way and are trapped by the wilderness. By turning south instead of taking the normal road, Israel looked confused and helpless to the king of Egypt. God used this very appearance of weakness to draw the tyrant into a trap.

God announces that He will harden Pharaoh's stubborn heart so the king will chase after Israel. Through the destruction of Egypt's army, God would win great glory and prove to everyone that He alone is the Lord. The Israelites obeyed God's unusual order and pitched their tents just as they were told.

When Pharaoh and his officers heard that Israel had truly departed for good, they instantly regretted letting them go. Now that the shock of the tenth plague had faded, they only cared about losing millions of free workers who built their cities. Their pride and greed quickly drove them to change their minds.

Pharaoh prepared his own royal war chariot and gathered an elite force of six hundred chosen chariots, along with all the other chariots in Egypt. Each chosen chariot carried trained soldiers ready for swift battle. This formidable army moved rapidly to recapture the unarmed multitude.

The Lord allowed Pharaoh's stubborn heart to drive him forward in hot pursuit of the Hebrews. Meanwhile, the Israelites had marched out of Egypt boldly and with high hopes, confident in their new freedom. They had no idea that a fierce army was already racing after them.

The Egyptian army, with all its chariots, horses, and soldiers, quickly overtook the Israelites where they were camped by the sea. The people of Israel were resting at Pi-hahiroth with no human way of escape. What seemed like a peaceful camp suddenly turned into a place of great peril.

As the sound of the Egyptian chariots grew near, the Israelites looked up and saw their former masters marching straight toward them. They were completely terrified because they were unarmed, burdened with children and herds, and trapped against the water. In their panic, many of them cried out to the Lord for help.

The terrified people turned against Moses with bitter sarcasm, asking if he brought them out to the wilderness simply because Egypt lacked graves. They claimed it would have been far better to remain as slaves than to die in the open desert. Fear made them instantly forget the wonderful miracles God had just done for them.

Moses calmly told the trembling crowd not to fear, but to stand still and watch the Lord rescue them that very day. He promised them that the terrifying Egyptian soldiers they saw right now would never be seen again. Even before knowing how God would do it, Moses trusted God's promise completely.

Moses assured the people that the Lord Himself would fight the entire battle for them. Their only job was to be quiet and stop their anxious complaining. When people are at the very end of their own strength, God often steps in to do what only He can do.

The Lord asked Moses why he was crying out in silent prayer instead of putting the camp into motion. Prayer is necessary, but there comes a moment when faith must step forward into action. God ordered Moses to tell the people to start marching directly toward the water.

God commanded Moses to raise his staff and stretch out his hand over the sea to divide the water. This miracle would open an avenue of dry land right through the middle of the deep sea for Israel to walk upon. The staff did not possess magic power, but it showed that Moses was God's chosen leader.

God declared that He would make the Egyptians so blindly confident that they would march straight into the dry seabed after Israel. Through the complete defeat of Pharaoh and his army, God would reveal His supreme power and justice. When it was finished, Egypt would finally recognize that the Lord is the one true God.

The angel of God and the great pillar of cloud moved from the front of the Hebrew camp and took up a position behind them. This placed God Himself directly between His defenseless people and their oncoming enemies. The cloud that had guided them forward now served as a protective shield.

The pillar stood between the two camps all night long, bringing deep darkness to the Egyptians while shining bright light upon the Israelites. Because of this supernatural barrier, the Egyptian soldiers could not get close enough to attack during the night. God's presence brings comfort and light to His people, but confusion and trouble to those who oppose Him.

Moses stretched out his hand over the water, and the Lord drove the sea back with a powerful east wind that blew all night. The seabed was dried up, and the deep waters were split in two. God used the wind as His instrument, showing that all nature obeys His command.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars suggest the crossing occurred at a shallow marsh or reed lake, where strong seasonal winds and low tides naturally exposed the ground, rather than a miraculous division of deep water.

notes.meaning: The Israelites walked right into the midst of the sea on dry ground, with the waters standing like solid walls on their right and left sides. They marched safely through the night guided by the light of the pillar of fire. This miraculous passage protected an entire nation along with their elderly, children, and livestock.

Driven by rage and blinded to danger, Pharaoh's horsemen and chariots charged straight onto the seabed after the Israelites. They were so intent on catching their prey that they rushed into the very path God had carved out. Presumption and stubbornness led them into an inescapable trap.

Just before daybreak, the Lord looked down on the Egyptian army from the pillar of fire and cloud and threw them into wild panic. A flash of divine presence or sudden terrifying judgment broke their ranks and filled them with dread. God can instantly turn the proudest army into a confused and helpless crowd.

The Lord caused the chariot wheels to twist and break, making the vehicles drag heavily in the muddy seabed. In sheer terror, the Egyptian soldiers shouted that they must turn and run, because the Lord Himself was fighting for Israel against them. They realized the truth only after it was already too late to escape.

Once the Israelites had crossed safely, the Lord told Moses to stretch his hand out over the sea again. This action gave the signal for the divided waters to come crashing back upon the Egyptian chariots and cavalry. The very element that had provided a path of salvation for Israel would become a grave for their oppressors.

Moses stretched out his hand at daybreak, and the waters returned with full force to their normal level. The panicked Egyptians tried to run away from the surging waves, but the Lord swept them straight into the sea. Daylight made God's judgment visible for all to witness.

The returning waters completely covered the chariots, horsemen, and the entire army of Pharaoh that had entered the seabed. Not a single soldier among them survived the flood. God fully dismantled the military power of Egypt in a single morning.

While the Egyptian army was wiped out, the Israelites had walked completely unharmed on dry ground with walls of water on both sides. This contrast highlighted the difference between those whom God protects and those who fight against Him. God makes a safe path through impossible obstacles for those who trust Him.

On that decisive day, the Lord completely delivered Israel from the control of Egypt, and the people saw the bodies of their pursuers washed up on the beach. Seeing their enemies dead confirmed that their former slavery was truly ended forever. God left no doubt that His people were free.

When the Israelites saw the immense power the Lord displayed against Egypt, they were filled with deep reverent fear toward God. They put their trust in the Lord and believed in Moses as His true messenger. Witnessing God's mighty rescue turned their complaints into faith and praise.
